Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the RetailFlow Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. There will be an opportunity to ask a question after the presentation. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to RetailFlow Inc.'s Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Taylor Kim, COO; and Morgan Patel, CMO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, CEO of RetailFlow Inc.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q2 performance, driven by exceptional mobile app engagement metrics and the early success of our new product launches like SphereFresh, VirtuFit, and EcoSphere. We saw significant growth in key metrics, with gross merchandise value reaching $15.2 billion, up 8% year-over-year, and mobile commerce now accounting for 62% of total GMV.

Our focus remains on expanding our take rate through smarter pricing and promotions while navigating macroeconomic headwinds like inflation and higher interest rates. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our advertising efficiency improvements, where ROAS has climbed to 7.2x. We believe this will significantly enhance our profitability trajectory.

We are investing heavily in operational excellence, including advanced fulfillment networks and AI-driven personalization.

Finally, we are committed to delivering sustainable growth for our customers and shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. Our Q2 revenue was $3.4 billion, an increase of 12% year-over-year. Gross margin was 45%, driven by take rate expansion, improved product mix toward higher-margin categories, and efficiencies in our fulfillment services. Operating expenses were $2.0 billion, representing 59% of revenue. Our marketing investments remained disciplined, with total spend at $308 million yielding strong returns, as I'll detail shortly.

Our net income for the quarter was $400 million, or $1.20 per share. We ended the quarter with $5.0 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance of $14 to $15 billion in revenue and adjusted EBITDA margins of 18 to 20%.

Before moving to operations, let me provide deeper color on several key drivers of our performance, starting with one of our core growth engines: mobile app engagement, including downloads, active users, and conversion rates. In this hyper-competitive e-commerce space—where giants like Amazon, Shopify merchants, and TikTok Shop are vying for share—our app-first approach has been transformative. Mobile drove 62% of our total GMV this quarter, up from 55% last year, in line with eMarketer forecasts that m-commerce will reach 44% of U.S. retail e-commerce by year-end.

On downloads, we achieved a record 4.2 million new installs, up 28% year-over-year and 12% quarter-over-quarter—our best since Q4 2022's holiday peak. iOS accounted for 58% or 2.4 million, Android 42% or 1.8 million, reflecting our U.S. and APAC emphasis where Android holds 75% share per Statista. This growth stemmed from precise user acquisition, with ROAS on install campaigns at 4.2x, improved from 3.5x last year via Meta and Google Ads optimized for SKAdNetwork 4.0 and Apple's tracking changes. We directed 35% of our $45 million digital marketing budget to app-focused creatives, like 15-second unboxing videos for hits such as wireless earbuds and athleisure, boosting organic downloads 15% through ASO—we ranked #17 in U.S. Shopping on Google Play and #23 on the App Store.

North America led with 2.1 million downloads or 50% of total, thanks to Prime Day carryover and back-to-school pushes. APAC jumped 45% YoY to 1.2 million via India and Indonesia localizations like JioMart bundles and Shopee-style flash sales. EMEA grew 18% to 850,000, though GDPR slowed it; UK geofencing pilots should help. For the full year, we target 18-22 million downloads, emphasizing contextual installs through Apple Search Ads and Google's Performance Max.

Shifting to active users, where retention builds our moat: Monthly Active Users hit 18.5 million, up 32% YoY and 9% QoQ, beating guidance. Daily Active Users reached 6.2 million for a 34% DAU/MAU ratio, Weekly Active Users 12.8 million—outpacing Wayfair's 25% and Etsy's 28% DAU growth per App Annie. Retention cohorts improved: Day-1 to 42% from 38%, D7 to 28% from 24%, D30 to 16% from 13%. Key was our FlowLock personalization engine on AWS SageMaker, delivering 1.2 billion daily recommendations based on history, AOV, and sensors—lifting session depth 22% to 8.7 pages.

Tech upgrades included a May native redesign with SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose, cutting load times 40% to under 1.5 seconds per New Relic. Push notifications at 65% opt-in, like abandoned cart nudges with 18% recovery, added $28 million in revenue. AR try-on for 500+ fashion items boosted Gen Z engagement 35%, now 41% of DAU. U.S. MAU grew 25% to 9.8 million via RetailFlow Rewards with 14 million members and 5x app-exclusive points. APAC MAU soared 55% to 5.2 million with gamified features like Daily Spin wheels. EU/EMEA steady at 3.5 million, churn down 8% post-DMA-compliant updates. App serves as omnichannel hub, syncing with 1,200 kiosks for 27% higher cross-channel LTV at $156.

On conversion rates—orders per session—app hit 4.8%, up 18% YoY and 7% QoQ from Q1's 4.5%, topping web's 2.9% and Adobe's 3.2% industry average. Mobile generated 68% of our $1.4 billion quarterly revenue, with $68 AOV yielding $302 million app GMV. Checkout conversion was 72%, via one-tap Apple/Google Pay at 85% of transactions and PricePulse dynamic pricing for 12% CR lift without margin hits. Browse-to-cart rose to 22% from 19%, abandonment fell to 41% with exit-intent modals using reviews and timers. Post-iOS 14.5, privacy modeling kept 92% attribution, CAC at $12.40 per install. AR/VR converted 6.2% vs. 4.1%, live shopping streams hit 7.1%. U.S. CR at 5.3%, APAC 4.9% strong in electronics with vivo/Xiaomi ties, EMEA 3.9% improving via Klarna/iDEAL. Apparel dipped 2% from inflation, offset by grocery bundles up 14%.

These interconnect: app users show 2.8x LTV ($156 vs. web $56), 1.9x AOV, 47% less churn. FY24 capex of $120 million targets edge computing for 6% CR by Q4, with PWA capturing 15% web-to-app. Risks like ad volatility and Apple fees exist, but 75% app GMV margins protect us. Q3: MAU 20-21 million, downloads 4.8-5.2 million, CR 5.0-5.3%; full-year mobile drives 25% revenue growth.

Next, our new product and service launches contributed 12% to GMV growth. SphereFresh, same-day grocery in 15 U.S. metros using AWS robotics and RL forecasting, hit $250 million GMV in 90 days, beating $180 million target by 39%. AOV $85, 22% above core, with 15.2% session CR up 28% from real-time Kafka syncing cutting out-of-stocks 40%. NPS 72 vs. Forrester's 45, 4.8/5 stars from 1.2 million reviews praising 95% on-time 2-hour delivery. Repeat 62% in 30 days, LTV/CAC 4.2x. NY/LA 60% volume, Sun Belt pilots higher AOV.

VirtuFit AR try-on for 5,000+ SKUs like Nike/Levi's via ARKit/ARCore: 3.5 million users or 18% fashion traffic, 35% add-to-cart lift, 27% return reduction vs. 30-40% industry. $420 million GMV lift or 8% category. 4.7/5 from 850,000 reviews, NPS 68 for body scanning inclusivity; viral TikTok hit 2M views. APAC 25% penetration via Shopee/Lazada, 40% higher engagement; EU GDPR addressed with opt-in. Retention 55% MoM.

EcoSphere 500-SKU sustainable privates like organic cotton/recycled goods with blockchain verification: $180 million GMV at 120% plan, 45% margins from Vietnam/Bangladesh sourcing. 75% sell-through vs. 60%, via Impact Score badges. 4.9/5 stars, NPS 75 from 650,000 reviews on transparency; 70% Millennial/Gen Z. U.S. 65%, Europe 30% MoM on Green Deal, LATAM pilots 20% AOV uplift.

Cross-sells like SphereFresh-EcoSphere lifted AOV 15%, VirtuFit data boosts recs 22% CTR. $500 million FY24 for SphereFresh to 50 cities, VirtuFit to beauty/eyewear, EcoSphere to 2,000 SKUs targeting 20% GMV by FY25. Q3 pre-orders up 35%.

Turning to take rate, our blended rate expanded to 19.2%, up 110 bps YoY from 18.1% and 40 bps QoQ from 18.8%—fifth straight quarter, adding $280 million revenue on $42.5 billion GMV base, 8% of $8.2 billion total revenue. Ex-Prime Week, 19.5%.

By segment: Marketplace (82% GMV) 16.8% up 90 bps on electronics (22.4%) and home (20.1%) growth; fashion 14.2% up 60 bps. Fulfillment (SFN) 4.7% from 4.2%, 68% top seller penetration. Ads 5.9% up 150 bps, ARPU $1,450 up 22%.

Regions: NA (55%) 20.5% up 130 bps on premium services; Europe (25%) 17.8% up 80 bps despite DSA/DMA; APAC (15%) 16.2% up 50 bps vs. price wars; ROW 15.9%.

Drivers: Pricing (60 bps)—tiered fees (Pro 17-18%, Enterprise 20%+), 35% adoption, GenAI engine cut undercutting 12%. Promotions (30 bps)—Prime Week compressed 50 bps but rebounded; seller-funded capped at 25%. Other: mix shift (electronics 28%), fraud cut saving 30 bps, offsite ads +60 bps.

FY target 19.8-20.2%, 200+ bps expansion with 14% GMV/18% revenue growth. $500M FY24 automation for SFN >5.5%.

On macro impacts, inflation at 5.2% CPI eroded AOV 4% to $48, essentials up 22% to 35% GMV, discretionary down. Rates curbed >$100 orders 15%, but BNPL up 28%. NA up 12% to $8.4B resilient; Europe flat $3.8B on energy; APAC +15% $2.3B led SEA/India; LATAM +18%. FX shaved $450M GMV.

Mitigations: AI recs +11% CR/$1.2B GMV, Smart Logistics 85% fast delivery -20% churn, privates 18% GMV at 35% margins, dynamic pricing +7% rev/order. FY GMV 7-9%, revenue 11-13%, take 23%.

Finally, advertising efficiency: ROAS 7.2x up 24% YoY from 5.8x, T12M 6.8x on $308M spend yielding $2.1B revenue, 14.7% GMV cost.

Channels: Search/DSP 9.1x (Google/Amazon DSP); Social 6.2x Meta/5.8x TikTok; Emerging 12.3x NovaAds/7.5x CTV. US 8.1x +28%, EU 6.7x +19%, APAC 5.9x +15%.

Drivers: ML bidding 92% auto +22% lift/18% CVR; CDP 78% addressability +25% ROAS; mix to social/retail media 55%. Q3 7.4-7.6x guide.

Now I'll turn it over to Taylor to discuss operations.

Taylor Kim:
Thanks, Jordan. Operationally, we focused on scaling our Smart Logistics Network and enhancing supply chain resilience. Our shipping times improved by 25% year-over-year, with 85% of deliveries same- or next-day in key markets. Fulfillment costs declined 15% per unit through robotics and demand forecasting. We are implementing advanced edge computing with Cloudflare Workers for real-time inventory syncs across our micro-fulfillment centers.

Now I'll turn it over to Morgan.

Morgan Patel:
Thanks, Taylor. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from our Prime Week event and social commerce pushes like TikTok Shop integrations. Customer acquisition costs held steady at $12.40 overall. Our brand awareness increased by 20% per Nielsen metrics. We are focusing on first-party data strategies and retail media expansion through NovaAds to drive sustainable growth.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator instructions for Q&A session]. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On mobile app engagement, can you expand on the retention improvements and how FlowLock is contributing to LTV?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, Ben. Great question. As Jordan detailed, our retention cohorts have strengthened significantly—Day-1 at 42%, D30 at 16%—thanks to FlowLock's 1.2 billion daily personalized recs. This has driven app LTV to $156, 2.8x web, solidifying our competitive edge.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen:
Hi, team. Given the macro headwinds, how are you thinking about category shifts and private label role in FY24?

Jordan Lee:
Hi, Lisa. Inflation pushed essentials to 35% GMV up 22%, while we ramp privates to 18% at 35% margins. Dynamic pricing and BNPL have stabilized AOV, supporting our 11-13% revenue guide despite softer discretionary.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with JPMorgan.

Mike Patel:
Thanks. Taylor, on ops, what's the latest on SFN penetration and international expansion plans?

Taylor Kim:
Mike, SFN hit 68% with top sellers, mirroring efficient models but faster onboarding. Internationally, we're expanding micro-centers in SEA and Europe, targeting 5.5% take contribution via automation.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Lee with Barclays.

Rachel Lee:
Good afternoon. Morgan, thoughts on ROAS sustainability heading into holidays, especially with new launches?

Morgan Patel:
Rachel, our 7.2x ROAS reflects optimized mix—12.3x on NovaAds—and AI bidding. Holidays will leverage TikTok/Prime halo; we're guiding 7.4-7.6x Q3, scaling retail media for 15x potential.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
